findings.issue_summary: App displays an authentication screen and login flow for user accounts.
findings.evidence: In src/components/AuthScreen.tsx:28-70, the app renders an authentication interface supporting email login/registration (loginWithEmail/registerWithEmail) and Google sign-in. In composeApp/src/androidMain/kotlin/network/AuthHelper.kt:5, Firebase authentication state is retrieved via FirebaseAuth.getInstance().currentUser?.uid.
findings.recommendation:
Administrative Console Requirements: Because your app implements a login flow, you MUST complete two manual setup steps in the Play Console dashboard to pass review:
1. Reviewer Demo Credentials: Submit active, non-expiring test credentials so Google Play reviewers can access your gated features.
2. Account Deletion Link: Submit a public-facing web link for account deletion to satisfy Google Play's data deletion policies.

findings.issue_summary: App manages user accounts but lacks an in-app account deletion mechanism.
findings.evidence: The app handles user accounts via AuthScreen.tsx (lines 28-70) and AuthHelper.kt (line 5), but no UI component, screen, or API exists across the codebase to allow users to request account deletion or purge remote user data.
findings.recommendation: Implement in-app deletion: Create a highly discoverable path (e.g., under User Profile/Account Settings) to let users initiate account deletion directly in the app.
